title: Error Geometry and the Teacher's Advantage
subtitle: PolarGD · AOPD · Safety-probe scaling · Reading GD's max-margin bias
intro: Three main readings connect spectral geometry, distillation signals, and label budgets; 11 briefs cover inference allocation, data selection, and technical blogs. The classic derives GD's max-margin direction from logistic regression.

articles.paper: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
articles.authors: Egor Shulgin · Sam Laing · Antonio Orvieto · Peter Richtárik
articles.title: Exact polar: the error spectrum controls progress
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-21 14:01 EDT · v1; October 23 listing
articles.evidence: Read Sections 2-4, Theorems 1/3, finite NS, and the 90M-model experiment; no reproduction

blocks.text: Exact line search compares directions on matrix quadratics without learning-rate scaling effects. The analyzed PolarGD has no momentum.[1]

blocks.tex: f(E)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(E^\top HE),\quad G=HE,\quad E=X-X^\star,\quad H\succ0,\quad E\in\mathbb R^{d\times m},\quad \operatorname{rank}(E)=d\le m
blocks.label: Fixed left Hessian; full row rank is required below
Theorem 3: nuclear norm determines one-step decrease
Proposition 2: the error matrix determines preconditioner conditioning

blocks.text: If EE^T=cI, p(E)=1 gives one-step convergence. Even with H=I, nearly rank-deficient errors can make PolarGD much slower than GD. Finite NS amplifies tiny singular values approximately linearly instead of lifting them directly to one.[1]

rows: H=I, d=10, initial singular values 1 and 10^-4; exact-polar loss ratio 0.64 after its first step; GD finishes in one
90M Transformer, 1.8B tokens; roughly 1/4 of attention-momentum singular values lie in the five-step NS linear regime
blocks.caption: The latter establishes that this spectral regime exists, without testing end-to-end gains from fewer NS steps.[1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Quadratic line-search results do not directly cover nonconvex stochastic training with momentum. Greedy per-step progress need not produce the best trajectory.[1]

articles.paper: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation
articles.authors: Mahdi Sabbaghi · George Pappas · Hamed Hassani · Adel Javanmard
articles.title: AOPD: teacher-preferred tokens may not help the student
articles.evidence: Read Section 3, Lemma 3.1, external-teacher experiments, and Table 1

blocks.text: Let S be the frozen student rollout policy, T the teacher, R terminal reward, and H trajectory length. Q^S is expected reward after action a followed by student continuations; V^S averages over student actions. Weight teacher supervision by student advantage:[2]

blocks.tex: A^S(h,a)=Q^S(h,a)-V^S(h),\qquad J(\theta)=\mathbb E_{h\sim d_S}\sum_a T(a\mid h)A^S(h,a)\log S_\theta(a\mid h)
blocks.label: An irrelevant fixed trajectory-length constant is omitted

blocks.text: Separate continuations for every teacher action are unnecessary. Student trajectories and a baseline b independent of that trajectory, such as a leave-one-out mean, estimate the entire objective:[2]

blocks.tex: \widehat J=\frac{R-b}{H}\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\left[\frac{T(a_t\mid h_t)}{S(a_t\mid h_t)}\log S_\theta(a_t\mid h_t)-\sum_aT(a\mid h_t)\log S_\theta(a\mid h_t)\right]
blocks.label: Equation 3.6: unbiased if T>0 implies S>0; S, T, and history distributions are frozen

blocks.caption: Math / coding use 450 / 350 iterations, Qwen3-4B-Instruct / 8B teachers, and G=4 for both distillation methods.[2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Experiments clip ratios at c=4 and apply identical, unnormalized truncation to the teacher-sum term, modifying the target. Sampling temperatures differ across methods; the table does not isolate the objective's causal contribution.[2]

articles.authors: Yuchen Wu (University of Washington) · Jerry Wei (Anthropic)
articles.title: Safety probes: estimate the floor before buying size or labels
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-21 23:43 EDT (October 22 on arXiv) · v1
articles.evidence: Read Sections 3-5, fitted forms, and limitations in Appendix B

blocks.text: Probes read a fixed model's activations to detect safety attributes. Monitored-model size and labels form distinct budget axes. Six harder datasets reduce saturation seen on existing small datasets.[3]

blocks.label: Empirical fits: N is billions of parameters, D labels; CC++ uses g=1, while last-token probes fit g

blocks.tex: D_0=\frac B{\sqrt N},\qquad D_{\rm target}=\frac B{\sqrt N}\left(\frac{0.5-E_\infty(N)}{E_{\rm target}-E_\infty(N)}-1\right)^{1/g},\qquad E_\infty(N)<E_{\rm target}<0.5
blocks.label: D0 halves the chance-to-floor gap; the second expression algebraically inverts the fitted law

rows: Refit constants per family / task / probe
Predicting the next size from smaller models
72% of predictions miss by at most 0.02
73% choose the cheaper option under N times D cost
blocks.caption: Budget cases require both options to reach the target and measured costs to differ at least twofold.[3]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: An empirical AUROC law does not guarantee reliability at a fixed low false-positive rate. N times D omits actual labeling prices. The joint CC++ Qwen2.5 fit has RMSE 0.030 and maximum error 0.115.[3]

articles.paper: Direct Pass@k Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
articles.authors: Mahdi Salmani · Adel Javanmard · Devansh Gupta · Meisam Razaviyayn
articles.title: Thought pruning: optimize the pool's probability of any success

blocks.text: Maximizing pass@k of retained reasoning prefixes combines quality and redundancy in one objective. Across eight open-weight models it beats quality- or diversity-based heuristics, especially for moderate retained pools; the abstract gives no budget-matched numerical comparison.[4]

articles.paper: Random Remasking Scales Masked Diffusion Inference
articles.authors: Zhaoyi Zhou · Frank Wu · Andrea Zanette
articles.title: R-squared-D: remask-denoise as an inference-scaling axis

blocks.text: A Markov chain over clean sequences motivates inference-only R-squared-D; TCT additionally trains on trajectory errors. Logical tasks show near-log-linear scaling, over 97% on hard Sudoku and over 99% on 3-SAT. These results cannot all be attributed to training-free R-squared-D alone.[5]

articles.paper: High-Value Training Data from Noisy, Diverse Sources
articles.authors: Hedi Driss · Evan Frick · Anastasios N. Angelopoulos · Cho-Jui Hsieh · Yejin Huh · Tijana Zrnic · Andrew Ilyas
articles.title: Dataweights: transfer learned weighting rules to larger models

blocks.text: Metagradients learn example weights against a small high-quality target set. Parametric weighting rules extend to new or streaming examples and larger models, with reward-modeling experiments on human/synthetic mixtures. The abstract establishes no universal cross-scale transfer guarantee.[6]

articles.paper: Towards Faithful Data Selection: Statistical Limits and Scalable Algorithms
articles.authors: Ahmed Mehdi Inane · Mahdi Haghifam · Gintare Karolina Dziugaite · Ioannis Mitliagkas
articles.title: Replace unverifiable subset optimality with full-data faithfulness

blocks.text: Population-optimal selection requires a validation set larger in order than training data. Under ULA training, accumulated gradient discrepancy bounds KL between subset- and full-data-trained parameter distributions. Accepted swaps reduce that bound, without guaranteeing monotonic improvements in population error.[7]

articles.paper: Width and Depth Limits Commute During Training
articles.title: Width-depth training limits: clipping changes the convergence mode

blocks.text: For linear ResNets with 1/sqrt(depth) Depth-muP scaling and muP width parameterization, any fixed clipped-GD horizon has the same L2 limit along all joint growth paths. Without clipping, only convergence in probability is established; nonlinear networks and long horizons are outside this result.[8]

articles.paper: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale
articles.authors: Arvid Frydenlund · FuTe Wong · Katherine Lambert · Frank Rudzicz
articles.title: A graph-search scaling wall can depend on supervision and tokenization

blocks.text: Multi-token prediction and alternative tokenizations address separate barriers to shortest-path generation on unseen graphs. Authors report learning at larger graph scales than prior limits. This controlled latent graph-search result is not a general law of natural-language reasoning.[9]

articles.paper: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing Omega-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift
articles.authors: Edric Castel C. Hao · Juan Raphael S. Seña · Neon S. De Jesus
articles.title: One matched spectral statistic does not predict synthetic-data transfer

blocks.text: Across LSTM, PatchTST, and TCN with three seeds, Omega-matched sine-plus-noise pretraining improves mean ETTm1 MSE by 2.3%, whereas matched chaotic-ODE sources worsen it by 13.2%. The negative result concerns source selection, not synthetic pretraining in general.[10]

articles.paper: Predictable performance is suboptimal, and what it means for model routing
articles.title: Before routing inference, compare the predictor with self-confidence

blocks.text: A predictor's advantage over chosen-answer confidence transfers exactly to log-loss improvement through recalibration. Across 16 models and four benchmarks, predictor-based prediction and cascading gains shrink after finetuning. Predictor capacity must be counted in the comparison.[11]

articles.paper: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
articles.authors: Tuhin Kundu · Microsoft and Hugging Face collaborators
articles.title: ThinkingBox: repeatable success rises while coverage slips
articles.evidence: Read training, task-selection, and evaluation sections of the original blog

blocks.text: After 50 GRPO steps on a separate training pool, Qwen3.8-27B is tested 20 times on each of 507 tasks. Pass@1 rises 51.70% to 60.78%; observed 20/20 tasks rise 38 to 107, but pass@20 falls 89.35% to 87.97%. Observed 20/20 is not a deployment-reliability lower bound.[12]

articles.paper: A Good Self-Teacher Meets the Student Where They Are: Joint On-Policy Learning and Teaching
articles.authors: Randy Ardywibowo · Arnav Dalal · Jiantao Jiao
articles.title: JOLT: train the teacher to meet the student's capabilities
articles.dateNote: New blog October 21; paper arXiv:2610.10447 v1 first posted October 7
articles.evidence: Read original-blog methods and token accounting; the older paper is not counted as a new preprint

blocks.text: One model jointly learns as a privileged teacher and unprivileged student. Teacher rewards are regularized toward the student; JOLT+ adds student rewards. At 63.44% MATH accuracy, GRPO's observed 8.40M processed tokens are compared with JOLT's fitted 1.30M. The 6.5-fold token comparison is not wall-clock acceleration.[13]

articles.authors: Xingjian Bai · Jia-Hao Liang · Jayden Teoh · Vincent Sitzmann
articles.title: OPAL: rewrite Muon / AdamW recipes during a training run
articles.evidence: Read blog experimental settings, update logs, and cost discussion

blocks.text: An agent rewrites groupwise update code from training statistics, including Muon switches, momentum changes, and loss-spike guards. Multilingual NanoGPT and diffusion experiments compare available one-run recipes; RAEv2-B FID improves 3.39 to 3.19. Agent tokens and decision overhead must be counted; uniform compute superiority is not established.[14]

classic.paper: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Separable Data
classic.authors: Daniel Soudry · Elad Hoffer · Mor Shpigel Nacson · Suriya Gunasekar · Nathan Srebro
classic.title: Why does unregularized GD select maximum margin?
classic.dateNote: First posted 2017-10-27; JMLR 2018; read the binary sections of arXiv v7 (2024-10-26)
classic.evidence: Read the setting, Theorem 3, proof sketch, and degenerate-data discussion; no multiclass result is used

recognition.label: JMLR 2018 · Foundational historical work on implicit bias

classic.question: When the preconditioner P_t keeps changing, what testable conditions still yield a max-margin characterization in a fixed norm?

blocks.text: Hard-margin SVM explicitly selects small norm; separable logistic regression has no finite minimizer. Soudry et al. (2018) connect them: GD's norm diverges while its direction is selected.[15,16]

blocks.label: Finite, separable data; homogeneous linear predictor; X has columns xi; summed logistic loss has beta=1/4

blocks.text: This is the paper's asymptotic intuition, not a convergence proof. Assuming a limiting direction u, exponential tails suppress larger-margin examples, leaving support vectors.[15]

blocks.tex: -\nabla\mathcal L(w)\sim\sum_i e^{-y_iw^\top x_i}y_ix_i,\qquad \frac{e^{-g\,y_i u^\top x_i}}{e^{-g\,y_j u^\top x_j}}\to0\quad\text{if}\quad y_i u^\top x_i>y_j u^\top x_j,\quad g\to\infty
blocks.label: Logistic derivative's exponential tail; the ratio compares dominance along a fixed direction
The surviving nonnegative combination has SVM's KKT structure; direction convergence still needs proof

blocks.tex: w_t=\widehat w\log t+\rho_t,\quad \|\rho_t\|=O(\log\log t),\quad \left\|\frac{w_t}{\|w_t\|}-\frac{\widehat w}{\|\widehat w\|}\right\|=O\!\left(\frac{\log\log t}{\log t}\right)
blocks.label: Theorem 3: residual is at most log log t, and bounded for almost every dataset

blocks.title: Boundary and discussion
blocks.text: The general directional rate is slow; nondegenerate data improve it to O(1/log t). Arbitrary deep networks and Muon are not covered. When P_t changes, what testable conditions preserve a fixed-norm max-margin characterization?[15]
